1.note: Here and in the next verse, Ezekiel is providing background information to help readers understand the context of when and where he was when he received the visions from Yahweh. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **thirtieth**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year thirty]

The implication is that **in the thirtieth year** refers either to Ezekiel’s age at this time. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in my thirtieth year of life]

The **fourth** month of the Hebrew calendar, the month of Tammuz, includes the last part of June and the first part of July on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

In this verse, the word **exile** is singular in form, but it refers to all the Israelites who had been exiled to Babylon as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “exile.” Alternate translation: [the exiles]
The word **Kebar** is the name of a river south of Babylon.

Here Ezekiel is speaking as if the sky were a door or curtain that could be **opened**, allowing him to see into the heavenly realm. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The sky seemed to open like a curtain being pulled back] or [God allowed me to see into the heavenly realm]

This could mean: (1) Ezekiel saw **visions** that came from **God**, that is, visions that God gave him. Alternate translation: [visions that came from God] or (2) Ezekiel saw **visions** in which he saw **God** himself. Alternate translation: [God’s very presence]

2.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **exile**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the time when they carried King Jehoiachin away as a captive]

3.note: Ezekiel is using the term **word** to represent what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the message that Yahweh gave]

Ezekiel is repeating forms of the verb “be” translated as **being was** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [certainly came]

Even though Ezekiel is speaking about himself, he refers to himself in the third person as **Ezekiel, son of Buzi**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person here, and in the rest of the verse. Alternate translation: [to me, Ezekiel, son of Buzi]
The **land of the Chaldeans** is another way of describing the Babylonian empire as the Chaldeans ruled in Babylon.
Ezekiel is using the word translated as **And it was** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here, **the hand of Yahweh** represents “the power of Yahweh.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh powerfully worked in him there]

4.note: Ezekiel is using the term **behold** to focus his readers’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and there before me was]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a **wind** that was so strong it was considered a **storm**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a stormy wind]

This could mean: (1) a supernatural fire that was not burning an object but just burning within itself, Alternate translation: [and fire caught onto itself] or (2) a fire that was flashing back and forth like lightning. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and fire flashing continually back and forth]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **brightness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And bright light shone all around]
Here the pronoun **it** could refer: (1) to the brightness, Alternate translation: [and the middle of that brightness] or (2) to the cloud. Alternate translation: [and from the midst of the cloud]

Ezekiel is using **the eye of metal** as a common expression of the culture to mean the gleam that one would see shining, in this case, from metal in a fire. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was like the shining of metal]

The word translated as **metal** refers to a kind of shining substance whose exact identity is uncertain. It could refer to: (1) a shiny metal, such as bronze. The ULT and UST follow this interpretation. (2) a shiny stone, such as amber. Alternate translation: [was like the eye of amber]

5.q: דְּמ֖וּת אַרְבַּ֣ע חַיּ֑וֹת וְ⁠זֶה֙ מַרְאֵֽי⁠הֶ֔ן דְּמ֥וּת אָדָ֖ם לָ⁠הֵֽנָּה
5.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **likeness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [was something that resembled four living beings. And this was their appearance—they each resembled a man]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **appearance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And this is how they looked]

7.note: In the original language, the word for **foot** was more general and could include the leg. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And their two legs were straight]

In the original language, the word for **palm** was more general and could apply to either hands or feet. You could use the term that fits best in your language. Alternate translation: [but the soles of their two feet were like the hooves of a calf]

Similar to the phrase in verse 4, Ezekiel is using **the eye of polished bronze** as a common expression of the culture to mean the gleam that one would see shining, in this case, from polished bronze. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [likely highly polished shiny bronze]

8.note: The implication is that the hands of the beings looked like the hands of a human being. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And his hands looked like the hands of a human being]

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And this is what the faces and the wings of the four of them were like]

9.note: By **were each joining to its sister**, Ezekiel means that each being’s wings touched the wings of the beings on either side of it, so that together the four beings formed a connected group. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [each touched the wing of the being next to it]

By **each went toward his faces**, Ezekiel means that each being moved straight forward in the direction that one of its faces pointed, without turning. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [each one moved straight ahead in the direction that one of its faces pointed]

10.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **likeness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And their faces looked like the face of a man]

The implication is that **the face of a man** was the one that faced forward, since Ezekiel locates the other faces on the right and on the left. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the face looking forward looked like the face of a man]

11.note: Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [So, that is how their faces appeared]

The expression **were spread** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And they spread out their wings from above]

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [two wings were joining the wings of the creatures on either side, and the other two wings were covering]

13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **coals of burning fire** and **torches** are glowing and blazing, so was the appearance of the beings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Their appearance glowed and blazed as burning coals and torches do]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **likeness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the beings looked like this]
The pronoun **It** refers to the fire that Ezekiel has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The fire was moving about between the beings]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a **brightness** that is characterized as being as bright as a **fire**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and it shone brightly with fire]

14.note: By **running and returning**, Ezekiel means that the beings were darting back and forth. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [were dashing back and forth rapidly]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the lightning strike** is sudden and swift, so were the movements of the beings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [moved as suddenly and swiftly as a flash of lightning]

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression using “behold” in 1:4. Alternate translation: [and there before me was]
The pronoun **its** refers to each of the beings. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [beside each of the beings with its four faces]

16.note: Similar to the phrase in verse 4, Ezekiel is using **an eye of topaz** as a common expression of the culture to mean the gleam that one would see shining, in this case, from a precious jewel. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was like a shiny precious jewel]

A **topaz** is a kind of precious stone that is yellow or golden in color. If your readers would not be familiar with what a topaz is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a yellow gemstone]

The implication is that all four of the wheels looked alike. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and all four of the wheels looked alike]

This could mean: (1) that the two wheels were at right angles to each other, so that they could go in any direction without turning. Alternate translation: [two wheels at right angles, one inside the other] (2) that the two wheels were concentric. Alternate translation: [a smaller wheel that is part of a larger wheel]

17.note: This could mean: (1) without rotating as in the UST (2) without pivoting. Alternate translation: [they did not pivot]

18.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **height**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they were high]

Here, **fear** represents the awe that the wheels inspired in anyone who saw them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they inspired awe in anyone who saw them]

20.q: יֵלֵ֔כוּ שָׁ֥מָּ⁠ה הָ⁠ר֖וּחַ לָ⁠לֶ֑כֶת וְ⁠הָ⁠אוֹפַנִּ֗ים יִנָּשְׂאוּ֙ לְ⁠עֻמָּתָ֔⁠ם
20.note: The pronouns **they** and **them** refer to the beings. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the beings went—the spirit was there to go. And the wheels ascended beside the beings]

21.note: The pronoun **they** refers first to the beings and then to the wheels. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [When the beings went, the wheels went; and when the beings stood, the wheels stood; and when the beings ascended]

22.note: A **vault** is a kind of arched structure that spreads out overhead like the sky. If your readers would not be familiar with what a vault is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [was an arched covering spread out overhead]

Similar to the phrase in verse 4, Ezekiel is using **the eye of the fearsome ice** as a common expression of the culture to mean the gleam that one would see shining, in this case, from ice that gleamed like crystals, so brilliantly that it filled anyone who saw it with awe. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [like the gleam of awe-inspiring ice]

The expression **being stretched** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [extending over their heads from above]

23.note: See how you translated the similar phrase “were each joining to its sister” in 1:9. Alternate translation: [each touched the wing of the being next to it]

24.q: כְּ⁠קוֹל֩ מַ֨יִם רַבִּ֤ים כְּ⁠קוֹל־שַׁדַּי֙ בְּ⁠לֶכְתָּ֔⁠ם ק֥וֹל הֲמֻלָּ֖ה כְּ⁠ק֣וֹל מַחֲנֶ֑ה
24.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **many waters**, **the Almighty**, **a crowd**, and **an army** make an overwhelming noise, so did the wings of the beings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as overwhelming as the noise made by many waters, by the Almighty when they moved, by a crowd, or by an army]
The pronoun **they** refers to the wings of the four living creatures. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [like a sound of the Almighty when the wings moved]

By **their wings slackened**, Ezekiel means that the creatures lowered or relaxed their wings when they stopped moving. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they dropped their wings]

25.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **And it was** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated this same phrase, “their wings slackened,” in the previous verse.

26.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a stone of sapphire** is deep blue and gleaming, so was **the likeness of a throne** that Ezekiel saw. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [was the likeness of a throne, deep blue and gleaming as a sapphire stone]

A **sapphire** is a kind of precious stone that is deep blue in color. If your readers would not be familiar with what a sapphire is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a deep blue jewel]

26.q: דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א וְ⁠עַל֙ דְּמ֣וּת & הַ⁠כִּסֵּ֔א דְּמ֞וּת כְּ⁠מַרְאֵ֥ה & אָדָ֛ם עָלָ֖י⁠ו מִ⁠לְ⁠מָֽעְלָ⁠ה
26.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **likeness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [was something that resembled a throne, and on the thing that resembled the throne was something that looked like a man on it from above]

26.q: וְ⁠עַל֙ דְּמ֣וּת & הַ⁠כִּסֵּ֔א דְּמ֞וּת כְּ⁠מַרְאֵ֥ה & אָדָ֛ם עָלָ֖י⁠ו מִ⁠לְ⁠מָֽעְלָ⁠ה

27.note: See how you translated the same phrase, “like the eye of metal” in 1:4. Alternate translation: [something like the shining of metal]

The word translated as **metal** refers to a kind of shining substance whose exact identity is uncertain. It could refer to: (1) a shiny metal, such as bronze. The ULT and UST follow this interpretation. (2) a shiny stone, such as amber. Alternate translation: [was like the eye of amber]

The pronoun **his** refers to the figure who looked like a man, whom Ezekiel described in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from the appearance of that man-like figure’s waist and upwards]

28.q: כְּ⁠מַרְאֵ֣ה הַ⁠קֶּ֡שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בֶ⁠עָנָ֜ן בְּ⁠י֣וֹם הַ⁠גֶּ֗שֶׁם
28.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a rainbow that is in a cloud on a day of the rain** is radiant with color, so was the brightness that surrounded this figure. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as radiant with color as a rainbow that is in a cloud on a day of the rain]
The pronoun **It** refers to the brightness. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [This brightness showed]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **likeness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [looked like what represented the glory of Yahweh]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how glorious Yahweh is]

Falling face down on the ground was a symbolic action by which Ezekiel showed his reverence and worship. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote.
